analysis:
The PR change in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 980-1027) adds documentation for an excluded startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). It is a docs-only change. The supplied units are BASE text with no changed lines on the base side, so I reviewed the surrounding calibration section (base lines 946-1016) and the patch excerpt, which is truncated.

Security-relevant behavior described in the excerpt:
- The warmup runs a greedy 128-token probe twice and, only on a cold-cache signal, runs shape cells.
- It uses the artifact's default sampling and a 20 s wall budget.
- Probes and cells train no rates or counters.
- Preemption leaves the warmup due.

Threat-model fit:
- The warmup is local-only, synthetic and excluded from measurement. It sends no customer data and crosses no coordinator trust boundary (TB-002).
- It consumes no consumer prompts (A-001) and creates no new network or disk surface.
- Prefix cache and SSD KV behavior (T-041) is not touched. The excerpt does not say whether warmup prompts could be donated to the SSD prefix cache. Calibration probes are described elsewhere as uncached, so this is plausible but unverified.
- Availability (T-010/T-029): the 20 s budget and preemption by customer requests (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.beginForeground) are documented as bounding impact.

Remaining integration questions for the actual Swift implementation, which is not in this batch:
- Warmup prompts must not be donated or persisted to the encrypted SSD cache.
- Warmup must not produce served-request counters or billing evidence.
- The retry-on-preemption path must be bounded.
- The third-try acceptance must not loop.

This PR adds no concrete security regression.
